options: Magenta dye (basic fuchsine) decolourised by SO₂
questions.explain: Bisulphite from SO₂ adds to the central carbon of fuchsine, breaking its conjugation and leaving a colourless reagent that turns magenta-pink with aldehydes.

questions.q: Which compound does NOT give a positive Schiff's test, even though its open-chain formula has a –CHO group?
questions.explain: Glucose exists almost entirely as a cyclic hemiacetal, so little free –CHO is present. This false negative is classic evidence for its ring structure.

questions.q: Why must Schiff's test be done cold and read within about a minute?
options: Heating drives off SO₂ and speeds up the slow reaction of ketones, both of which can give pink without an aldehyde
Heating destroys the aldehyde before it can react
Warm Schiff's reagent oxidises aldehydes to acids, which are colourless
The magenta adduct is stable only above room temperature
questions.explain: Loss of SO₂ restores colour to the reagent on its own, and ketones react very slowly to give the same colour, so heat or a long wait gives false positives.

questions.q: Schiff's test can be used to distinguish which pair?
questions.explain: Propanal (an aldehyde) turns the reagent magenta-pink while propanone stays colourless. Schiff's test cannot tell aliphatic from aromatic aldehydes, and glucose and propanone are both negative.
